text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn summed up the weekend congress of the Socialist Party in Budapest by urging the party to continue present policies.
- Horn has submitted an application to extend a special summer session of Parliament up until July 31.
- A draft on next year's parliamentary election campaign proposes a shorter campaign in which allocated campaign funds would be set at Ft 1 million per candidate.
- Minister of Agriculture Frigyes Nagy said in Mezohegyes (SE Hungary) at the weekend that foreigners have acquired six to seven percent of cropland through illegal "pocket" contracts.

- The National Bank (NBH) may consider cutting interest rates further if inflationary pressure continues to decrease and the rate of inflation drops to the targeted level, NBH president Gyorgy Suranyi told Reuters Financial Television in Basel.
- The current account showed a surplus of $19 million in March.
- The NBH is set to sell its 34 percent stake in CIB by September at the latest.
- The first round of privatization of national broadcaster Antenna Hungaria is expected to take place this year with an invitation for bids in September.
- The 780 million forints all-time record lottery jackpot has been won on Saturday.
- Annual inflation dropped below 18 percent in May, as compared to 18.6 percent calculated for April, analysts polled by Napi Gazdasag claim.
